The polynomial modulo q^(6n)-1 agrees exactly with the orbit-character polynomial. Polynomial positivity was also diagnosed for n=1 through 40, without treating a known positivity theorem as a new result.

I also verified the 4→7 multiplier by hand for every n. Let m = 8(n+3) and k = 2n+5. Then (2n+5)² = 4(n+2)(n+3) + 1, which is 1 mod m if n is even and 4n+13 ≡ −(4n+11) if n is odd. Also (2n+5)(2n+7) = 4(n+3)² − 1, which is 4n+11 if n is even and −1 if n is odd. So k·{±1, ±(2n+5), ±(2n+7)} = {±1, ±(2n+5), ±(4n+11)}. The 4→8 case is analogous with k = 2n+7. Multiplication by a unit is a graph isomorphism of circulants, so Classes 4, 7 and 8 are the same graph family up to isomorphism.

"statement": "A **polyomino** is a finite union of edge-connected unit squares in the plane. A set of queens is **independent** when no two queens attack each other, and it is **maximal dominating** when it dominates every square and no queen can be added while preserving independence.

**Maximal independent queen domination conjecture.** The maximal independent queen domination problem on polyominoes is NP-complete.

The conjecture asks whether the queen analogue of the known polynomial-time rook result becomes NP-complete already in dimension two. The paper reports extensive computations supporting this expectation, but no reduction is given.",

"statement": "Let $\gamma$ be an indifference graph, and write its chromatic quasisymmetric function in the elementary symmetric-function basis as

**The e-positivity conjecture.** For each $\gamma \in \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}$, $X_{\gamma}(\mathbf{x};t)$ is $e$-positive; equivalently, $a_{\lambda}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}[t]$ for every partition $\lambda$.

"title": "Induced-subgraph family conjecture for gap-free graphs",

"statement": "For each integer $n\geq2$, consider families of graphs $\{G_i^{(n)}\}$. A graph is **gap-free** when it has no induced subgraph consisting of two disjoint edges, and $I(G)$ denotes its edge ideal.

**Induced-subgraph family conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq2$, there exists a family of graphs $\{G_i^{(n)}\}$ such that $I(G_i^{(n)})^k$ has a linear resolution for all $k\geq n-1$, and whenever $G$ is a gap-free graph with $\reg(I(G))=n$, each $G_i^{(n)}$ is an induced subgraph of $G$.

"title": "NP-completeness of minimal queen completion on chessboards",

"statement": "Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $Q$ be a set of $k$ queens placed on an $n\times n$ chessboard. For a nonnegative integer $l$, the minimal chessboard domination queen completion problem asks whether there is a set $Q'$ of size $k+l$ such that $Q\subset Q'$ and $Q'$ dominates the chessboard.

**Chessboard queen completion conjecture.** The minimal chessboard domination queen completion problem is NP-complete.
